clue.text: Ring, then call round anyway, : being in the area

indicators.note: turned round any which way, so the ring and the word call are jumbled together

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone told to ring and then call round regardless, since they live nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round anyway' shuffles O (the ring) with CALL. 'Call round' reads as one idiom for visiting, but 'round' belongs with 'anyway' as the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby or neighbourhood-based is described as belonging to that place.

clue.text: Many a one criticised .the way women are today

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
I is the Roman numeral for one
berated means scolded

explanation.surface: Many women have been criticised for the modern way they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's liberation in the twentieth century freed women from many traditional restrictions.

clue.text: Instrument is nothing more than an electricity generator

indicators.note: the nothing is added on top of the generator, so it follows it

parts.note: a cell is a unit of a battery that produces current
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that some instrument is merely a dynamo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is nothing more than' reads as a sneer, but it means O added after CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: He works in service, but won't take orders

definitions.text: He works in service, but won't take orders

parts.words: He works in service, but won't take orders
parts.note: a church layman who leads parts of worship but is not ordained a priest

explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a servant and 'won't take orders' suggests disobedience, but it is a church service and holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson licensed to conduct some church worship without being an ordained cleric.

clue.text: Gives up solid food

parts.note: to drop a habit is to give it up
a cone is a solid figure in geometry

explanation.surface: Someone abandons solid food, as on a diet or after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solid' looks like an adjective for the food but is a noun: a geometric solid. A drop scone is a small thick pancake, also called a Scotch pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small griddle pancake, eaten as a teatime snack.

clue.text: How to prepare young fish from the sea?

indicators.note: the young fish come from the sea, so the sea is written first

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
fry are newly hatched fish

explanation.surface: A cook wonders how to prepare small fish just caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a cooking question; the first three words define a cooking method.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersing food in hot oil is a common method of cooking fish.

clue.text: Dealing with criminal assault

parts.note: of can mean concerning or about
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: A court case concerning a violent criminal attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal assault' reads as one phrase, but 'criminal' is the receiver of stolen goods and 'assault' alone is the definition, in the attacking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport and war the attacking side is on the attack, as opposed to defence.

clue.text: Gold pen lying around: — to create this?

definitions.text: Gold pen lying around: — to create this?

indicators.note: the pen lies around the gold, enclosing it

parts.note: a sty is a pig pen
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A writer with a gold pen tells fibs to make up a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone with a pen, lying, makes up a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a made-up account, and a fib or lie is also called one.

clue.text: To make from instructions needs application

indicators.note: the making comes from the instructions, so the instructions are written first

parts.note: orders are commands or instructions
to form is to make or shape

explanation.surface: Manufacturing to a set of instructions requires a formal request.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed sheet filled in to request goods is a kind of written request.

clue.text: If your number's up, it's his decision

definitions.text: If your number's up, it's his decision

parts.words: If your number's up, it's his decision
parts.note: the machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers, nicknamed like a man

explanation.walkthrough: 'your number's up' usually means death, but here it means your bond number is drawn. ERNIE is the computer that picks British Premium Bond prize winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects which savings bonds win prizes.

clue.text: Army rations are first-rate, but complaint follows

indicators.note: the complaint comes after the first-rate part, so it is written second

parts.note: bully is a dated word for excellent, as in 'bully for you'
a beef is a grumble

explanation.surface: A soldier says the army food is excellent, then immediately grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is tinned corned beef, a classic British army ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned corned beef was the standard field provision issued to soldiers.

clue.text: School dentist's extraction long ago

indicators.note: extraction says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A school dentist pulling a tooth from a child, recalled as something from years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraction' fits the dentist picture as pulling teeth, but here it pulls letters out of 'School dentist's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden times are bygone days, a period in the distant past.

clue.text: Note about not being paid short for the wine

indicators.note: the note goes around the outside of the shortened word

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
honorary means unpaid, and its short form is Hon.

explanation.surface: A musician, unpaid, is a little short of money for a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps RE round HON. 'short' makes HON the standard abbreviation of honorary, an unpaid position.
explanation.definitionFit: Côtes du Rhône and other wines are named after the French river valley where they are made.

clue.text: Goodness — 1 dn. is avoiding an engagement

parts.note: Fancy! is an exclamation of surprise, like Goodness!
the answer to 1 down means released, which is a synonym of unattached

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a liberated woman is dodging getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 dn.' points to the 1 Down answer, which means set loose; take a synonym of it. 'Goodness' looks like a noun but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fancy-free is not in love or committed to anyone, so they steer clear of betrothal.

clue.text: One in seven used to fall in the river

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river

indicators.note: the word used collapses and its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a person who once tumbled into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' reads as the past habit, but 'used' is the anagram fodder and 'to fall' its signal; 'One in seven' sounds like a statistic, not a day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the seven days that make up a week.

clue.text: Periodical meeting

definitions.meaning: a magazine; a well-known British literary monthly
a coming together, often by chance

explanation.definitionFit: Encounter was a famous Anglo-American literary magazine, and the word also means a chance coming together.

clue.text: Some daring to take advantage

definitions.meaning: a single bold deed or adventurous feat
to use something or someone selfishly for gain

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a bold feat; as a verb it means to use something unfairly for profit.

clue.text: Failing agricultural diploma?

parts.note: old university slang for being failed in an exam, plus the farm work of turning soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' was old Oxford slang for failing an exam, so this looks like failing a farming qualification while naming a farming job.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning furrows is farm work, and to be ploughed was student slang for flunking an examination.

clue.text: Are you proposing in the old-fashioned way? How very touching!

definitions.text: Are you proposing in the old-fashioned way?
definitions.meaning: archaic second-person verb form after thou, meaning you offer or put forward

explanation.walkthrough: To tender is to offer, and the old second-person form after 'thou' adds -est.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic grammar gives 'thou offerest' this form, and it is also the superlative of soft-hearted.

clue.text: Type of art with spirit and delicacy

parts.note: Art Deco is a style of design from the 1920s and 1930s
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: An art style is praised for its vigour and refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delicacy' means tact and propriety here, not a tasty morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe tactful, proper behaviour and good manners.

clue.text: Oratorio is a disaster — needs to be harmonious all round

indicators.note: the harmonious word goes right round the jumbled letters

parts.note: gears that mesh fit together smoothly

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the words is a in ruins, rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic pans an oratorio performance and says it must be more tuneful throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' tempts as MESS, but that leaves the end unexplained: here it shuffles 'is a', and 'needs to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Messiah is the most famous English choral work of its kind.

clue.text: Soldier servant

definitions.meaning: an infantryman, one who fights on foot
a liveried attendant in a grand household

explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant an infantry soldier and also a uniformed household attendant who waits at table.

clue.text: Room for amusement when a' ruffian gets beaten up

indicators.note: the thug's letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug gets thrashed at a place of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' means space rather than a chamber: a funfair is an outdoor fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with rides and stalls provides space for entertainment.

clue.text: Woman who fell in the yard — she has a pain, all from the back

parts.note: a court is an enclosed yard or courtyard

indicators.note: take the back letter of every one of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman who tumbled in a courtyard is in pain, with her back hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all from the back' takes the last letters of 'she has a pain', giving ESAN. 'Woman who fell' means a fallen woman, not one who tripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallen woman was the old moral term for one living as a kept mistress of wealthy men.

clue.text: Students may be working

definitions.meaning: a group taught together at school
working is one kind of social stratum

explanation.definitionFit: A group of pupils taught together is one meaning, and 'working' is a social stratum it can describe.

clue.text: Sailor goes on to raised deck

parts.note: a tar is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor climbs onto the upper deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TO into OT. 'deck' is a pack of cards, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards form a special pack used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Old cricketer's style

definitions.meaning: W. G. ..., the famous Victorian English batsman

explanation.definitionFit: W. G. Grace was a legendary Victorian cricketer, and the same word means elegance of manner.

clue.text: Make a note to acquire church vestment

indicators.note: the note takes on the church at its end

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
CE is short for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is told to write down that the church must buy a priest's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' just sets the scene for writing a note; 'church vestment' reads as one phrase, but 'church' gives CE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a white linen cloth worn round the neck by a priest at Mass.

clue.text: Nearer the back in pursuit

definitions.meaning: comparative of aft, toward the stern of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Read as aft plus -er it means closer to the stern; as a preposition it means chasing behind.

clue.text: To make Roman? Yes and no

definitions.text: To make Roman? Yes and no

parts.words: To make Roman? Yes and no
parts.note: printers' sloping type is named after Italy, home of Rome, yet it is the opposite of upright roman type

explanation.walkthrough: In printing, roman is upright type and italic is sloping type, so putting words in italics both does and does not make them 'Roman'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set text in sloping type is Italian in name, but it takes it out of roman typeface.

clue.text: On which some of Procrustes' victims were removed?

definitions.text: On which some of Procrustes' victims were removed?

parts.words: On which some of Procrustes' victims were removed?
parts.note: Procrustes racked short guests to fit his bed; an injured person is carried off on a litter

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Procrustes stretched short guests to fit his bed; a casualty is carried away on a portable litter of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas litter carries injured people away, and the word also suits a device for lengthening bodies.

clue.text: Glamorgan opener moved to another county.

indicators.note: the opening letter of Glamorgan, like a batsman who opens the innings

parts.note: went is the past tense of go, meaning moved

explanation.surface: Glamorgan's opening batsman transfers to a different county cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan and Gwent are Welsh counties, and Glamorgan is also a county cricket club, so 'opener' suggests a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwent is a historic county in south-east Wales, a neighbour of Glamorgan.
